The defining quantitative feature of these ETFs is structural: Shariah screens force a permanent zero-weight on Financials and a heavy tilt to Technology (35–42%), Healthcare and Energy — so any model that ignores tech-factor and quality-factor dynamics will systematically misprice them.

Under the MSCI Islamic Index Series methodology (October 2024 / May 2025 versions), three ratios must all stay below thresholds:

A 30% (vs 33.33%) tighter "entry buffer" applies to new constituents to reduce turnover. Existing constituents are removed only after exceeding the threshold for three consecutive index reviews ("exit buffer"). MSCI also operates an "M-Series" variant whose denominators are 36-month average market capitalization rather than total assets — used by S&P/Dow Jones Islamic indices and the Invesco IGDA. A non-permissible revenue cap (≤ 5%) applies to mixed-activity firms, and a
factor is applied to total-return calculations so income derived from impermissible sources is mathematically donated.
MSCI methodology is certified by an independent Shariah advisory committee that issues a periodic fatwa (since March 2007 per MSCI's published methodology documents).
No interest/coupon-bearing assets at fund level
— cash management is restricted to non-interest-bearing accounts or Shariah-compliant money-market instruments.

SECTION 4 — Recommended Forecasting Models and Pipelines
For each model below I list: (a) why it suits halal ETFs, (b) Python libraries, (c) features/engineering, (d) strengths/weaknesses, (e) references.
4.1 Classical time series — ARIMA/SARIMA and GARCH

ISWD, ISDE and IGDA show clear volatility clustering (squared-return autocorrelation), and weekly/monthly returns exhibit slow mean reversion. Khairunnisa, Rodoni & Rama (2024) successfully applied ARIMA to six Shariah indices and concluded they are EMH-weak-form-compliant (predictable by historical data). For volatility specifically, GARCH-family models dominate (Akbar, Bhutto & Rajput 2021; the
Volatility Patterns of Islamic Equity Funds
statsmodels.tsa.arima.model.ARIMA, statsmodels.tsa.statespace.SARIMAX, arch (Kevin Sheppard) for GARCH(1,1), EGARCH, GJR-GARCH, TGARCH; pmdarima.auto_arima for grid search of (p,d,q).
Log-returns; first-differenced log-price; squared returns for variance modeling; calendar dummies for quarterly rebalances.
Interpretable; well-suited to weekly horizons; GARCH gives one-step-ahead conditional variance for VaR/risk overlay. Asymmetric variants (GJR-GARCH, EGARCH) capture the leverage effect.
Linear; cannot use exogenous features cleanly without SARIMAX; assumes stationarity which fails at regime changes; mean-equation R² typically very low for equity returns.

4.2 ML — XGBoost / LightGBM with financial features

Gradient-boosted trees handle non-linearities, missing data, mixed feature types, and have dominated the M4/M5 forecasting competitions. They excel at directional classification (sign of next return) which is the practically useful signal for halal ETFs given low expected return spread.
xgboost, lightgbm, catboost, scikit-learn, mlforecast, optuna for hyperparameter tuning.

Lagged returns (1, 5, 10, 21, 63 days); rolling vols and Sharpe ratios at multiple horizons; technical indicators (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Z, ADX) computed with pandas-ta or ta-lib; macro features (VIX, USD index, TED spread proxy, 10Y Treasury yield, Brent oil) via FRED; sector-rotation features (XLK, XLV, XLE relative strength) as proxies for Islamic-overweight sectors; FX (DXY, USDCHF for ISWD.SW); cross-asset signals (gold, BTC); calendar features (day-of-week, month-end, quarterly-review dummies).
Robust to feature engineering experimentation; SHAP values give feature attribution; handles non-stationarity via re-training in walk-forward; very strong for medium-term (weekly–monthly).
Doesn't learn temporal structure inherently (must be encoded via lags); prone to overfitting in financial data; needs careful walk-forward CV.

4.3 Deep learning — LSTM and Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)

Halal ETFs are heavily exposed to a small set of mega-cap tech names whose news flow and earnings cycles drive most of their variance. LSTMs capture sequential structure; TFTs add interpretable multi-horizon attention and can ingest static covariates (e.g., "this is ISWD" vs "this is IGDA") to share learning across the three Islamic ETFs.

tensorflow.keras / pytorch for raw LSTM; pytorch-forecasting (Lim et al. TFT implementation) — see official TemporalFusionTransformer class; darts (Unit8) which wraps NHITS, TFT, NBEATS, TCN behind a sklearn-style API; neuralforecast (Nixtla) for fast TFT/NHITS.

Static categorical = fund_id (ISWD/IGDA/ISDE); time-varying known = day-of-week, days-to-quarterly-rebalance; time-varying observed = OHLCV, factor returns, macro indicators; targets = log-return at horizons 5, 21, 63 days.
TFT outputs quantile forecasts (uncertainty bands), variable importance and attention weights — useful for academic interpretation. NeuralProphet/NHITS also strong on monthly horizons.
Data-hungry — ISWD has only ~18 years of daily data (~4,500 obs) and IGDA only ~4 years (~1,000 obs), risking overfitting; black-box; expensive to retrain in walk-forward.

The best published results on financial forecasting are hybrids — e.g. GARCH residuals fed into LSTM, or stacking ARIMA + XGBoost + LSTM. Empirical Asset Pricing via ML (Gu, Kelly, Xiu 2020) shows ensemble methods dominate single models.

4.5 Factor models — Fama-French / Carhart adapted for Islamic indices

The literature is clear — Islamic equity returns are well-described by a 3- to 5-factor model with sign-flipped value (HML negative because financials/value excluded), positive momentum, and a strong investment factor (CMA) loading (Safiullah & Shamsuddin 2021,
; Abdul Halim 2023). For long-horizon forecasting, factor-conditional expected returns are more stable than raw price forecasts.
statsmodels.regression.linear_model.OLS, linearmodels (Sheppard) for panel and risk-factor regressions; pandas-datareader to pull Ken French data library; pyportfolioopt for Black–Litterman views.

Linear; assumes constant betas; ignores microstructure.
Fama & French (1993, 2015); Carhart (1997); Safiullah & Shamsuddin (2021) "Asset Pricing Factors in Islamic Equity Returns"; Girard & Hassan (2008).
